synopsis: EU acceptance of collision-mitigation systems runs through machinery conformity, and Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027, before the mid-2027 validation campaign [f2009, f10700]. The booklet identifies the EU as the most consequential jurisdiction found for machine-learning safety functions and recommends budgeting for notified-body involvement for EU sales after that date unless legal advice concludes otherwise; it separately reports a 2 August 2028 milestone for AI-specific machinery requirements under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [f2363, f2370, f12418, f2858]. Machinery conformity can admit analytical and simulation evidence through technical documentation, risk assessment and verification, rather than requiring every conclusion to come from proving-ground tests [f15095]. However, target markets are unspecified, so EU applicability remains unresolved: the EU was used as a reference because its dates are published, while non-EU markets would shift the primary legal context to their own rules [f10701, f11282, f11284, f11285]. For EU sales, the booklet recommends checking standards status immediately before the 2027 declaration because the harmonized list was unfinished in 2026; EN 474 harmonization, the status of the public-road non-road-machinery proposal, and the consequences of disabling automatic braking remain unresolved [f15084, f15247, f2950, f2953].

relations.note: Both identify Regulation 2023/1230 and its applicability before the mid-2027 campaign.
Both recommend planning notified-body involvement for EU machine-learning safety functions after January 2027.
Both classify EU regulations and other named regulatory rules as law, not standards.
Both prioritize US, Australian and South African rules when those are the target markets.
